title: Charles IX to Philibert du Croc, undated (1565–1567 or 1572), DECODE R2789

documents.shelfmark: Archives départementales de la Nièvre, fonds du Bourg de Bozas (exact cote not given by Destray)

plaintext.source: George Lasry's plaintext overlay, published by Satoshi Tomokiyo on Cryptiana on 25 May 2022

transcription.source: Destray's facsimile on Gallica (ark:/12148/bpt6k932364m, views f88 and f89, IIIF full size), signs labelled from George Lasry's key table of 25 May 2022 (cryptiana GL.htm)
transcription.notes: 14 Nov 2026: R2789_transcription.txt, 42 lines, 1622 signs (78 distinct labels) plus 34 vertical strokes; 1656 tokens with the strokes on _check_profile.py --measure --drop-first. 47 signs marked doubtful. A single AI transcription not checked by a person; look-alike signs (D1/O3, P1/F1/N2, E2/QUE, V4/LL/POUR, B1/S1) were labelled by sense, so those labels are not independent of the plaintext. The earlier READING.md is a copy of Lasry's overlay, not of the signs.

system.summary: A sixteenth-century French homophonic symbol substitution with special signs for common words, names, and titles.
system.sibling_key: Lasry's published key for this Charles IX–du Croc system; the 27 April 1567 Catherine de Médicis–du Croc letter uses a different symbol set.
system.notes: The classification and word-sign values come from Lasry's published overlay/key, not a key reconstructed in this project.

prior_solution.where: Satoshi Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, GL.htm, overlay supplied by George Lasry

conditions.human_role: The user logged in to DECODE, making the authenticated images available in the in-app browser.

solution.what: Opened DECODE R2789 with the user's authenticated session and exported both manuscript pages.
Read Destray's cited edition and found the same facsimile on Gallica; it identifies the item as document XLIII, without place or date.
Followed the cited Cryptiana prior art and found George Lasry's complete-page plaintext overlays published in 2022.
Compared the DECODE scans, Destray's Gallica facsimile, and Lasry's overlays; page layout, signatures, and every visible line correspond.
Transcribed the published overlay diplomatically and normalized its secure substance, retaining all visible gaps and uncertain phrases.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): READING.md (the project's transcription of Lasry's overlay) and cryptiana GL.htm as decryptions; no ciphertext transcription (project work).
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Looked for an existing transcription of the cipher signs: none in the folder; DECODE R2789 public API record and record page carry two images and no transcription or document attachment; cryptiana GL.htm carries Lasry's key table and plaintext overlays as images, no sign transcription. The DECODE images (614 and 707 px wide) and Destray's facsimile on Gallica (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF, views f88 and f89, 3330 x 4796 px) were fetched without a login.

Transcribed both pages sign by sign from the Gallica facsimile, in 3-line crops, labelling each sign from George Lasry's key table (R2789_transcription.txt: 42 lines, 1622 signs, 78 distinct labels, 34 vertical strokes, 47 signs marked doubtful). Single AI transcription, not checked by a person; several look-alike pairs of signs were labelled by sense.

Decoded the transcription by its labels (R2789_decode.txt) and compared it with READING.md line by line: every line agrees with Lasry's overlay; where READING.md has a gap the decode mostly shows a word sign or letters (line r01 'QUE VOUS CONGNOISSES [TRES] BIEN L HVMEVR DE CEVLX A', r18 'QV IL N EN SERA RIEN CONCLVD QUE JE N EN SOIS PREMIE-'). Nine unknown signs (U1-U9) and the queried word signs stay unvalued. The sentence reading and translation were not redone.

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's plaintext overlays of both pages were on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm (25 May 2022) before the attempt; the work compared them with the DECODE R2789 scans and Destray's 1924 facsimile and transcribed the overlay.
outcome.notes: The prior solution reads the letter in substance but leaves several signs or short phrases unresolved. No new cryptanalytic solve is claimed.

texts.label: Charles IX to Philibert du Croc, undated (1565-67 or 1572)
texts.summary: Charles IX tells his ambassador in Scotland, Philibert du Croc, to use his judgment and follow his instructions for the country's peace; above all his nephew, the young James VI, is to be well brought up, keep the Scots' traditional attachment to France, and not marry before Charles has been told and can send his intention. The postscript orders him to keep the English from gaining a foothold in Scotland. READING.md is a working transcription of George Lasry's plaintext overlay published on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm (25 May 2022), with its gaps kept.
texts.note: Transcription (14 Nov 2026): R2789_transcription.txt, a single AI transcription of the signs from Destray's facsimile (Philibert Du Croc, 1924, doc. XLIII, Gallica), labelled with Lasry's key table and not checked by a person; R2789_decode.txt is its mechanical decode. The decode gives letters and word signs in several places where READING.md has a gap (it was copied from the overlay at low resolution); R2789_reading.md has not been redone from it. 24 Oct 2026: 92.8% of the words of R2789_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
